summary: Ishtar: Gardens of Babylon is a colorful tile-laying game about planting flower gardens whose shapes and connections matter, using a rondel-like structure to gather gems and place gardeners for end-of-round scoring. It's a light-medium euro puzzle where cutting off an opponent's garden link with a tree can be as important as your own growth.
criticised: can feel dry or overly mathematical for the pretty theme
availability of actions depends on card draws
runs a bit long relative to its depth at higher counts

interaction.kind: racing to claim flower/gem spots on a shared rondel-influenced board and buying trees to cut off opponents' links
interaction.detail: Players compete for the same limited flower and gem spots and can purchase trees specifically to block a link between two spots an opponent wants to use. Beyond that direct blocking, much of the scoring (upgrades, apprentices) is pursued on one's own track, so it's a shared board with real but intermittent conflict rather than constant fighting.

subsystems: garden/flower majority-control engine (flowerbeds and the fountains they connect to)
tree and skill purchasing economy (bought with gems earned from the garden engine)
sources: victory points per flower in flowerbeds you control
fountain-control bonus (largest connected flowerbed at each fountain)
points printed on purchased tree cards
bonus points from unlocked skill upgrades
scoring.how_you_win: Send apprentices to grow and control flowerbeds (scoring a point per flower and contesting majority control of the fountains those beds connect to), while spending gems earned along the way on tree cards and skill upgrades that add further points; when two of the vegetation-tile supply piles run dry the game ends and the highest combined total wins.
